note: Retrospective scan summary. The Phase 1 wiki expansion and Phase 2 arXiv/web scan for this task both completed and were committed (f9e8723 for Phase 1; dream_cycle/staged/2026-08-04/*.json for Phase 2) prior to this file being written -- a concurrent/duplicate trigger of the same 'Nightly trading research session' task ran and finished the actual research work, but the scan-summary JSON deliverable was never written before that session's context ended. This file reconstructs the summary from the completed research-log entry (wiki/trading/research-log/2026-08-04.md) and the 3 staged proposal JSONs, without re-running the search, per task-registry guidance against duplicate scans.
scope: Searched arXiv/web across the trading wiki's core themes (momentum, PEAD, LLM trading agents, regime detection, portfolio construction), explicitly avoiding jump models, earnings-call NLP, and Black-Litterman aggregation since those were already covered as of the 2026-08-03 scan.

findings.title: Beyond Agent Architecture: Execution Assumptions and Reproducibility in LLM-Based Trading Systems
findings.summary: Direct one-month follow-on to the reproducibility-crisis survey (arXiv:2605.19337) already in the wiki. Widens the audited sample from 19 to 30 studies and converts the diagnosis into an explicit 7-dimension coded evidence matrix (data provenance, temporal split discipline, execution timing, turnover treatment, transaction-cost modeling, point-in-time controls, universe/artifact release), plus a 10-equity worked example quantifying how much friction/timing choices alone move reported performance.

findings.title: QuantSightBench
findings.summary: Tests whether LLMs produce well-calibrated prediction intervals for continuous numeric quantities (vs. FinBench's categorical/classification confidence). 11 frontier/open-weight models; best (Gemini 3.1 Pro) hit only 79.1% coverage vs. 90% target; coverage falls below 65% at 100K+ magnitude. No George hypothesis yet has an LLM output a numeric estimate with an uncertainty band -- logged as a calibration prior for any future H279/H280/H281-family proposal.
findings.note: Also directly drove a full new wiki page created during Phase 1 (ai-industry/quantsightbench-interval-calibration-2026.md, committed in f9e8723), since the finding warranted a dedicated page rather than just an in-page note. The staged proposal is the companion cross-reference note.

findings.title: Agent framework ecosystem update (LangGraph production-adoption lead; CrewAI token-overhead benchmark)
findings.summary: Refreshes agent-frameworks-2026.md (unchanged since 2026-05-29). As of March 2026, LangGraph holds an estimated 40% production-deployment lead over competing frameworks and surpassed CrewAI in GitHub stars. CrewAI 1.14 (May-June 2026) shipped pluggable backends; an independently reported benchmark found CrewAI crews carry ~18% higher token overhead than an equivalent LangGraph implementation on a comparable 3-agent task.

cross_note: No new PEAD, regime-detection, or portfolio-construction angle cleared the staging bar this cycle beyond what was already logged or explicitly excluded by instruction (jump models, earnings-call NLP, Black-Litterman aggregation -- all covered 2026-08-03). Scan concentrated on LLM-agent-evaluation and calibration angles, which is also why the Phase 1 wiki expansion (AI Industry) and Phase 2 staged proposals ended up thematically aligned.
